Subject: FinTechCo — API authentication & key management (post-demo qualification)

Hi Sanjay / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align the technical sync with your infra/security teams.

Recap (from today)
- Use case: server-side calls to Redwood endpoints for document embeddings + reranking, plus occasional user-driven calls for chat/structured output.
- Traffic profile: spikes during batch ingestion windows; most queries are low-latency per-user requests.
- Primary concerns: key management/rotation, auditability (who called what and when), and ability to use service accounts for backend services.

Authentication / Key management options (what we discussed)
1) Service account (recommended for backend): JWT-based service account tokens issued by your identity system or Redwood-managed service accounts. Advantages: short-lived creds, better rotation, least-privilege scoping.
2) API keys (developer-friendly): simple header-based keys for quick tests or internal services. We recommend pairing with IP restrictions and automated rotation.
3) OAuth2 / OIDC (user-delegated): ideal for end-user consent flows. Redwood supports standard OIDC flows and token introspection.

Notes on implementation/ops
- Rotation: We recommend short-lived tokens (15m–1h) with automated rotation for private keys. Redwood integrates with KMS/HSM providers for key wrapping and rotation automation.
- JWKS / public keys: Redwood exposes JWKS endpoints and supports validating signed JWTs from your identity provider.
- Audit logging: request-level logs (token id, model/route, latency) can be pushed to your logging backend or exported to S3.

Integration/SDK notes
- SDKs (JS/Python): support passing api_key OR bearer token from a service-account JWT. We have examples showing automatic retry/batching for embeddings and a sample reranker pipeline.
- Routing & fallbacks: requests can be routed by region/latency or sent to a cheaper quantized variant for background jobs; we can share routing policy examples.
- Structured output/tool calling: Redwood supports tool calling patterns and structured JSON output; recommend schema-validated responses for downstream ingestion.

Attachments: I attached our integration guide and a short SOC 2 excerpt that should help your security team. Also linking our HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789

Proposed next steps
- Technical sync (infra + security): Tue Dec 7, 11:00 AM PT — 30m. Can you confirm?
- Provide security contact(s) and any questionnaire we should expect.
- I'll send a short pre-read (integration guide + SOC2 excerpt) to the security inbox.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Best,

Thanks Sanjay — confirmed for Tue Dec 7, 11:00 AM PT. Invite is sent.

Quick answers to your questions to prep the call: 
- Rotation cadence: recommended pattern is short-lived tokens (15m–1h) for minted JWTs. For long-lived credentials we recommend rotating the underlying private keys at least weekly and automating rollover. Redwood provides APIs and integrations with common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) to automate rotation and zero-downtime key rollout.
- JWKS / OIDC: Redwood supports consuming your OIDC metadata/JWKS from Okta/Keycloak and can also accept signed assertions. We also publish our JWKS for token verification where applicable.
- Audit logs / delivery: yes — request-level audit logs can be exported to your S3 bucket or streamed to your logging endpoint. We can add lifecycle/retention metadata as part of the export.

Prep for the call:
- Security will want the SOC 2 excerpt (attached) + our standard integration checklist — attached redwood-integration-guide.pdf.
- We'll run through a sample flow: service-account JWT issuance -> call to /embeddings -> reranker pipeline + tracing for audit. Ethan will join to walk the SDK snippets and routing examples. Dev will field any infra/network questions.

Next steps (post-call)
1) Security questionnaire completed by FinTechCo and returned to marissa@redwood.ai / dev_patel@redwood.ai.
2) If acceptable, we'll send a PoC access key scoped to a test project and a short-lived service account credential for integration testing.
3) Outline SLOs and expected traffic for Dedicated vs Hosted options (if you want capacity predictability).
